Join us for an evening of lush, intimate sound comprised of stringed instruments, vocal harmonies, and original compositions featuring local musician Meschiya Lake. 

ABOUT THE MUSICIAN 

Meschiya Lake is a dynamic addition to Asheville’s music scene, bringing her powerful vocals, captivating stage presence, and genre-spanning sound to audiences across Western North Carolina. After years of building an acclaimed career in New Orleans, Lake has made Asheville home, blending jazz, blues, Americana, and country influences into performances that are both timeless and fresh. Whether performing intimate originals or beloved classics, Meschiya’s heartfelt storytelling and infectious energy continue to win over local music lovers throughout the region. 

From the stages of Lincoln Center in New York City, to Brazil, Canada, Denmark, The Netherlands, Italy, Russia, the United Kingdom, and Ireland, Meschiya Lake has shown people to express love of life through music and dance.  This passion, seemingly tireless energy, and expert skill have garnered much praise, from NPR’s top ten albums of 2010 to First Lady of Jazz 2013, at the Sun Valley Jazz Festival. But most importantly, back at home in New Orleans, Lake was recognized as Female Performer of the Year, three years running, at the Big Easy Awards, and named Best Female Singer in Offbeat Magazine’s Best of the Beat poll in 2013 and 2014.

event.cost: Free for Members (pre-registration required) and $15 for non-members
event.description:
Step into the Museum’s galleries before the doors open for a quiet and contemplative morning of meditation, mindful walking, and reflection. This guided experience invites participants to slow down, settle the nervous system, and explore the Museum as a place of sanctuary, spaciousness, and renewal.

The session will begin with a brief seated meditation, followed by a walking meditation through selected exhibitions. Along the way, participants will pause with gentle mindfulness prompts designed to support personal reflection, embodied awareness, and a deeper connection with the artwork. Rather than offering art historical interpretation, the experience encourages each participant to notice what arises within them through presence, stillness, and mindful seeing. The group will honor noble silence throughout much of the session with occasional opportunities for brief reflection and sharing. No previous meditation experience is needed.

Join Joshua on October 3, November 7, and December 5.

Joshua Canter is a mindfulness meditation teacher and the founder of True Nature Travels and Education, an Asheville-based organization that has offered transformative retreats and educational experiences around the world for more than 20 years. He holds a master’s degree in Contemplative Psychology and is passionate about making mindfulness accessible, grounded, and relevant to everyday life.

event.description:
Your life is filled with textiles made from various spun threads and yarn. Come deepen those connections with the fibers that are deeply woven into many aspects of our lives by trying your hand at one of the earliest ways to handspin yarn using a drop spindle.

Join us for a fun, educational and meditative day of learning the top whirl dropspindle, and maybe some other styles as well. We will prepare, card and spin raw wool fleece to create yarn on a drop spindle. You may have time to try different types of fibers and even different types of spindles. You will get to take home your first handspun yarn, as well as a drop spindle to continue exploring this new skill.

ABOUT THE TEACHING ARTIST

Jamie Sparks is a multidisciplinary artist and educator with more than 30 years of experience teaching learners of all ages. She has spent more than two decades working with natural fibers, specializing in spinning and felting, and has taught throughout the Southeastern United States, including the John C. Campbell Folk School, Tryon Arts and Crafts School, assisting at Penland School of Crafts and numerous arts councils.  Her fiber arts instruction emphasizes the transformation of raw fleece into finished pieces, combining traditional techniques with an accessible, hands-on approach. Jamie holds an Associates in Metalsmithing from Haywood Community College, where she developed her skills in metalwork and design. Prior to her work in the arts, she focused life as a herbal educator and plant biologist with a focus on the relationship between humans and plants—a passion that continues to influence her creative practice.

event.title: In Conversation | An Artist Talk by Lesley Dill
event.cost: $10 for Members and $15 for non members
event.description:
Join us for an evening with New York-based artist Lesley Dill, whose work is featured in the current exhibition, The Art of Paper. Dill will talk about her projects that involve paper and collaboration, from huge community and large-scale installations to the intimate creation of artist books and sculptures, as well as her work with artists, poets, students, and studios, such as Tamarind and Dieu Donne. 

PAPER IS MY FRIEND: 

“Paper is about fingertip energy for me. The way one moves in to touch paper is like no other approach. It’s as if each finger has a little imaginary rocketship in it. We touch nothing else the way we touch paper. Paper is the medium of intimacy. The end result is wonder. All printmaking begins with the choice of what paper and in this way, it is about a relationship to fragility and force. This relationship comes from Poetry.” 

ABOUT THE ARTIST

Lesley Dill is an American artist working at the intersection of language and fine art in sculpture, printmaking, installation and performance, exploring the power of words to cloak and reveal the psyche. Dill has had over one hundred solo exhibitions. Her artworks are in the collections of many major museums, including the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Whitney Museum of American Art, and the Museum of Modern Art, New York. In 2017 she was named a fellow of The John Simon Guggenheim Foundation. Her opera, Divide Light, based on the poems of Emily Dickinson, was performed in San Jose in 2008, restaged in New York City in 2018, and captured in an award-winning film by Ed Robbins. Dill’s exhibition Wild Grace This Private Hallucinatory Moment at Arthur Roger Gallery in New Orleans (2025–26), a result of research conducted as a 2023–2024 Smithsonian Artist Research Fellow, examined themes of radiance and healing in seen and unseen energies. Dill’s exhibition Wilderness: Light Sizzles Around Me, organized by the Figge Art Museum and traveled to seven venues from 2021 to 2023, amplifies voices of the North American past as they wrestle with divinity, deviltry, and freedom, including Mother Ann Lee, Black Hawk, Sojourner Truth, John Brown, Emily Dickinson, Horace Pippin, and Sister Gertrude Morgan. Ms. Dill is represented by Arthur Roger Gallery in New Orleans. She lives and works in Brooklyn, New York. For more information and images of her work, visit www.lesleydill.net

event.title: Exhibition on Screen | The Curious World of Hieronymus Bosch
event.cost: $12 for Members; $15 for non-members (does not include Museum admission)
event.description:
Hieronymus Bosch – Visions of Genius at the Het Noordbrabants Museum (February 13–May 8, 2016) was the largest ever Bosch retrospective, bringing 36 of his 44 surviving works together in Den Bosch. The exhibition took a radical approach, offering research and conservation expertise in exchange for loans from the world’s best museums. Over 420,000 people flocked to the exhibition to marvel at Bosch’s curious creations, with opening hours extended to 1am to accommodate the phenomenal demand.

Accompanied by expert insights from the exhibition’s curators and leading cultural critics, the film delves into the life of the visionary artist to explore the inspiration behind his strange and haunting works. Contributors include maverick filmmaker and artist Peter Greenaway, The Times’ Chief Art Critic Rachel Campbell-Johnston, and Director of the Het Noordbrabants Museum Dr. Charles de Mooij.

The Curious World of Hieronymus Bosch allows audiences to appreciate the detail of Bosch’s paintings like never before, offering close-up views of the curiosities hidden within his brimming canvases, from cannibalistic clergymen to three- headed birds.

event.title: Adult Studio: Introduction to Papermaking
event.cost: $125 (Museum Members receive 10% discount with code at checkout; two partial scholarships for underserved populations; materials included)
event.description:
This workshop will give you hands-on experience working with several pulps to learn the basics of Western style mould and deckle papermaking.

Join us to learn:

  • how to process recycled and commercial fibers into pulp at home or in a paper studio.
  • what tools and equipment are needed for papermaking.
  • how to pull, press and dry sheets of paper.

The day will start with a discussion about papermaking and will explore a variety of handmade paper samples. Afterwards, we will set up vats of pulp and make sheets of paper together. Each participant will take home a stack of sample papers. It’s up to you how you use the finished sheets. All are welcome. No experience necessary.

ABOUT THE TEACHING ARTIST

Alyssa Sacora (she/her) is a crafts person working in plant-based mediums of papermaking, book arts, basketry, and weaving. She finds inspiration by observing relationships between plants and humans throughout time. To reduce her footprint and encourage creative thinking, she primarily works with locally available and repurposed natural materials. In addition to and in support of her craft, she tends a large garden in Fairview, North Carolina with fruits and vegetables, medicinal herbs, and art plants.

Alyssa has taught for a variety of organizations in Western North Carolina and often utilizes an outside setting to help her students make the connection that we are nature and that our lives are intertwined with the plants, the soil, and the air around us. To learn more about Alyssa, see her work and course offerings, visit www.thepatchworkunderground.com.

Southern Circuit screenings are funded in part by a grant from South Arts, a regional arts organization, in partnership with the National Endowment for the Arts. For more information about Southern Circuit please visit www.southarts.org/southerncircuit.

Screening time: 1:26:00

Film Synopsis:

After 20 years of chronicling his Puerto Rican family, a director and his mother craft animations that bring
their loved ones back to life.

About the filmmaker:

William D. Caballero is an American filmmaker whose work merges documentary, animation, and
handcrafted miniature worlds to explore memory, migration, faith, and the emotional architecture of
family. Across film, television, and short-form media, Caballero has developed a singular visual language
rooted in tactile set-building, intergenerational storytelling, and a deep reverence for his Puerto Rican
heritage.
In 2001, he was awarded the prestigious Gates Millennium Scholarship, recognizing his academic promise
and leadership at an early stage in his career. He went on to earn a BFA from Pratt Institute in 2006 and an
MA from New York University in 2008. This foundation in both fine art and cinematic storytelling laid the
groundwork for a practice that bridges visual art, documentary realism, and experimental fabrication.
While at NYU, Caballero created American Dreams Deferred, his first (but not last) autobiographical
feature about his family.

AmiciMusic returns with a thrilling program entitled “THE SOUND of AMERICA.” Pianist and Artistic Director Daniel Weiser will be joined by violinist Tim Schwarz from Philadelphia in this exciting exploration of the incredible diversity of our American sound.  The program includes Spirituals and Ragtime as well as Blues-inspired works by W.C. Handy and William Grant Still, the Native-American inspirations of Charles Cadman, the Jewish influence on Ernest Bloch, the country fiddling in Aaron Copland, and the Latin rhythms in Bernstein’s West Side Story.  Weiser and Schwarz served as the 1996 U.S. Artistic Ambassadors of Music for which they performed more than 50 concerts in 11 countries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia showcasing our American music.

AmiciMusic is a chamber music organization based in Asheville and Baltimore dedicated to performing the highest quality chamber music in intimate venues and non-traditional spaces. This concert breaks down barriers between performers and audiences by setting up a more relaxed and informal atmosphere through informative talks about each composer’s life before each piece is played.

Add a VIP Ticket: Round out your concert experience by joining us from 5:45–6-45pm in the Museum’s Perspective Café for a pre-concert reception. Meet the musicians and your fellow concert goers while enjoying a drink and some light bites. Premium reserved seating for VIP ticket holders will allow you to join the concert just before start time.

About the Musicians

Since his solo debut with the legendary Philadelphia Orchestra at age nine, violinist Timothy Schwarz has had a brilliant career as a soloist, chamber musician, and pedagogue. Praised for his “energetic performances” (Rome News) and “technique beyond reproach” (Buffalo Times), Schwarz regularly performs throughout Europe, Asia, and the Americas as a soloist and chamber musician. His many recordings include the 2018 release of Anthems from Prometheus (Albany Records) “All credit to Timothy Schwarz for providing a performance as gripping from first to last as this one” (Fanfare Magazine), the 2013 release of Early Chamber Works by Jennifer Higdon (Naxos) “Top 10 Classical Albums in 2013” (Philadelphia City Paper) and his 2006 release of Timothy Schwarz, Live! “Good enough to be the only recording in your collection” (American Record Guide).  An avid educator, Schwarz is currently Assistant Professor and Head of Strings at Rowan University and Artistic Director and Founder of Techne Music, which includes a summer chamber music camp and concert series. For a five-year period through 2001, Schwarz served three tours as Artistic Ambassador in South America, Asia, and Africa, performing over 100 recitals in 15 countries. He received a Masters of Music from the Peabody Conservatory and a Doctorate of Musical Arts in Performance from Temple University. For further information and a performance schedule, visit www.TimothySchwarz.com.

Daniel Weiser, pianist, has a Doctorate in Piano/Chamber Music from the Peabody Conservatory, where he studied with Samuel Sanders and Robert MacDonald and won the Richard Franko Goldman prize for outstanding contribution to musical and educational life. He has performed on many great stages, including the Weill Recital Hall of Carnegie Hall, the National Gallery of Art in Washington D.C., and on the Dame Myra Hess Concert Series in Chicago. He has also concertized around the world, including Israel, Thailand, Holland, and France and was the 1996 United States Artistic Ambassador Abroad, for which he performed on an eleven-country tour of the Middle East and Asia. He has been on the music faculty of Dartmouth College and the prestigious St. Paul’s School in Concord, New Hampshire.

event.description:
Two hundred years after its opening and a century after acquiring its first Van Gogh artworks, the National Gallery, London is hosting the United Kingdom’s biggest ever Van Gogh exhibition. Van Gogh is not only one of the most beloved artists of all time, but perhaps the most misunderstood.

This film is a chance to reexamine and better understand this iconic artist. Focusing on his unique creative process, Van Gogh: Poets & Lovers explores the artist’s years in the south of France, where he revolutionized his style. Van Gogh became consumed with a passion for storytelling in his art, turning the world around him into vibrant, idealized spaces and symbolic characters.

Poets and lovers filled his imagination; everything he did in the south of France served this new obsession. In part, this is what caused his notorious breakdown, but it didn’t hold back his creativity as he created masterpiece after masterpiece. Explore one of art history’s most pivotal periods in this once-in-a-century show. Made in close collaboration with the National Gallery.

event.title: Exhibition on Screen | Van Gogh: Poets & Lovers
event.cost: $12 for Members; $15 for non-members (does not include Museum admission)
event.description:
Two hundred years after its opening and a century after acquiring its first Van Gogh artworks, the National Gallery, London is hosting the United Kingdom’s biggest ever Van Gogh exhibition. Van Gogh is not only one of the most beloved artists of all time, but perhaps the most misunderstood.

This film is a chance to reexamine and better understand this iconic artist. Focusing on his unique creative process, Van Gogh: Poets & Lovers explores the artist’s years in the south of France, where he revolutionized his style. Van Gogh became consumed with a passion for storytelling in his art, turning the world around him into vibrant, idealized spaces and symbolic characters.

Poets and lovers filled his imagination; everything he did in the south of France served this new obsession. In part, this is what caused his notorious breakdown, but it didn’t hold back his creativity as he created masterpiece after masterpiece. Explore one of art history’s most pivotal periods in this once-in-a-century show. Made in close collaboration with the National Gallery.

event.title: Adult Studio: Ekphrasis at the Museum
event.cost_details_json: {"currency_symbol":"$75 (Museum Members receive 10% discount with code at checkout; two partial scholarships for underserved populations; materials included)","currency_code":"USD","currency_position":"prefix","values":[]}
event.description:
Ekphrastic writing is made in response to a piece of artwork. For example, it can be a poem jump-started by a painting, a short story inspired by a sculpture, or a micro-essay triggered by a collage. 

We’ll explore different forms of ekphrasis through writing exercises and prompts — the collections of the Asheville Art Museum as our muses. 

The purpose of this workshop is to generate new writing while also learning tips and tools for creating ekphrasis in other settings. Join us for a fun and inspirational adventure of creating in community with other art-loving writers! 

Alli Marshall is multi-genre writer with an MFA from Goddard College. Formerly an arts writer and editor for Mountain Xpress, she is now a certified Creative Facilitator and the author of How to Talk to Rockstars and The Persephone Project. Alli has taught creative writing courses though Story Parlor, Great Smokies Writing Program, Flatiron Writers Room, Revolve, and Inward & Artward.

The mission of Asheville Music School is strengthening communities through music education and outreach, while sustaining teachers and musicians in a vibrant music culture. event.title: South Arts: Southern Circuit Tour of Independent Filmmakers | Backside
event.cost: Free for Members or included with Museum admission
event.description:
Join us for a screening of Backside followed by a conversation with the filmmaker, Raúl O. Paz-Pastrana.

Southern Circuit screenings are funded in part by a grant from South Arts, a regional arts organization, in partnership with the National Endowment for the Arts. For more information about Southern Circuit please visit www.southarts.org/southerncircuit.

Screening time: TBD

Film Synopsis:

Backside offers an intimate portrait of the migrant workers who endure long hours and often dangerous
working conditions year-round to prepare polished horses for “two minutes of glory.”
With the support of an all Latinx team of talented filmmakers and groom experts, Backside took five
years to make. The film peels back the layers of Churchill Downs’ barns (In Louisville, KY), known as the
“backside,” patiently revealing the symbiotic relationship between human and animal labor. Across a full
racing season, the expertise and grit of the workers are juxtaposed against the wealth and pageantry of
the Derby, exposing entrenched disparities of race and class that remain very much a part of the fabric of
the United States. In its essence, Backside is an ode—to the working class, and most profoundly, to the
immigrant workers who quietly sustain this country.
In today’s political climate, immigrants are often dehumanized and blamed for the poverty, violence and
declining living conditions in our country, ills we did not create. Backside invites viewers to look beyond
these incendiary words, to meet the people whose stories are rarely told. It asks audiences to witness
their lives, their dignity, their resilience—and, in doing so, to reflect on the vital role immi-grants play in
our communities.

About the filmmaker:

Raúl is a Mexican immigrant filmmaker, cinematographer and multimedia creator traversing borderlands
and migrant trails. His work intersects narrative fiction, participatory filmmaking, and visual ethnography
to explore themes of belonging, alienation and the concept of “home.”
Raúl’s films include “Backside” (2025 Tribeca / FICM, 85min.) a feature film about the migrant workforce
behind the Kentucky Derby, exploring the relationship between the thoroughbred horses and those who
care for them; “Border South” (2019 Sheffield / FICG, 84min.), which follows the clandestine migrant
routes from southern Mexico to the U.S.-Mexico border; and “The Stars are the Same” (2025 Aspen
ShortFest 12min.), which focuses on the experiences of an Indigenous Mayan elder who fled war-torn
Guatemala for southern Colorado. His films have screened worldwide including at the Tribeca Film
Festival, Sheffield Doc/Fest, the Aspen ShortFest, the Margaret Mead Film Festival, MASS MoCA
Museum, the Guadalajara International Film Festival, and the Morelia International Film Festival (FICM),
among many more. His work has received support from the Princess Grace Foundation, The Ford
Foundation, the LEF Foundation, ITVS, Catapult Film Fund, the Jerome Foundation, and the Sundance Institute, among others. Raúl is a Firelight Media Documentary Lab Fellow, a New America National Fellow, a Creative Capital Awards Artist Fellow, and a Guggenheim Fellow.

event.cost: Free for members or included with Museum admission
event.description:
Join us for a screening of Bluff City Chinese followed by a conversation with the filmmaker, Thandi Cai.

Southern Circuit screenings are funded in part by a grant from South Arts, a regional arts organization, in partnership with the National Endowment for the Arts. For more information about Southern Circuit please visit www.southarts.org/southerncircuit.

Screening time: 44:00:00

Film Synopsis:

Two Chinese-American storytellers uncover the untold history of Chinese immigrants in Memphis,
Tennessee, across a 150-year tapestry of identity and resilience.

About the filmmaker:

Thandi Cai (they/them) Director and Creator of Bluff City Chinese identifies as a storyteller of the Asian
Diaspora. Cai grew up in Memphis, TN where they learned how storytelling could be used to empower
themselves and others across racial, political, gender, ethnic and economic lines. Cai uses visual arts,
film-making, and graphic design to begin conversations around critical dialogue. Their goal as an artist is
to arouse imagination, pleasure, and improvisation to ideate new paths forward.
After earning a BS in Architectural Design, they served for two years as an education volunteer for Peace
Corps Lesotho until 2018. From there they were a teaching-artist, exploring the intersection of nonprofit
work, art, and community organizing. In 2022, they earned an MFA in Visual Communication Design at the
School of the Art Institute of Chicago.

event.title: MACNY Future Women in STEM
event.description:
@

Explore careers in engineering, manufacturing, and science with amazing local women that work in these industries!

This free series for girls in 6th-8th grades brings female professionals from local companies to lead students in a fun, hands-on activity together to spark interest in high-tech careers.

Program includes FREE admission to the MOST (student and their family) and light snacks.

Learn more and sign up for FREE!

event.title: TACNY Junior Café Scientifique
event.description:
@

TACNY Junior Café Scientifique, a program for middle-school students, features discussions between STEM professionals/academics and students about topics in the fields of science, technology, engineering and mathematics in an informal atmosphere, and seeks to encourage students to consider careers in these areas. Students must be accompanied by an adult, and can explore the MOST at no cost immediately following the event. The program begins at 9:30, with continental breakfast available at 9:15. Attendees are welcome to spend the day at the MOST after the event.

See session details and RSVP information.
event.excerpt: Free program for students featuring presentations and activities with local STEM professionals

event.title: Sensory Friendly Time
event.description:
@

Featuring special sensory-friendly EEK = MC2 Halloween activities in our STEAM Cafe area from 9-11.

Sounds are turned down, air compressors are turned off, and lighting is adjusted to accommodate learners with neurodivergence or sensory-processing challenges. The early hours also help ensure that wait times and crowd sizes are reduced.

Free for members; $9/$7 for adult / youth & senior non-members (personal aides are always free)

Activities include DIY Bats, Creature Coloring Station, Monster Constellations, Monster Pixel Art, Monster Mask Photo Op, Mummification Station, Temporary Monster/Halloween Tattoos, Monster Builder Station, and Ghost Lollipop Maker

All activities free with admission.

event.title: FREE Film — America the Beautiful
event.description:
@

Special for Veterans Day, watch the debut of “America the Beautiful,” playing every hour on the half hour, from 9:30 through 3:30 in the National Grid ExploraDome. FREE for all guests!

Reserve Free Tickets

America the Beautiful is a sweeping giant screen experience celebrating the vast and varied natural worlds that define the United States and the conservation movement that has ensured their survival. The protection of America’s beauty, wonder and resources was set in motion by Theodore Roosevelt and other pioneers who popularized principles still in practice today, passed down through generations, that will keep America’s wild heart beating for many more. Audiences will embark on an awe-inspiring journey from sea to shining sea, across the country’s most iconic and diverse environments – soaring mountain ranges, expansive plains, surprising deserts, flowing rivers and wetlands – captured with the scale, clarity, and immersion of spectacular giant screen cinematography.

event.title: Rodrigo Teaser: Michael Lives Forever
event.description:
Step back into the golden era of pop music as Rodrigo Teaser brings the electrifying legacy of Michael Jackson to life in a one-night-only spectacular at Syracuse’s iconic Landmark Theatre.
This isn’t just a concert — it’s a full sensory journey through the career of the King of Pop. From the soulful energy of the Jackson 5 era to the record-shattering anthems of Thriller, Bad, and Dangerous, Rodrigo Teaser channels the voice, the movement, and the unmistakable charisma that made Michael Jackson a global icon. Every glide, spin, and gravity-defying lean is meticulously recreated, transporting the audience straight back to the sold-out arenas and legendary performances that defined a generation.
Backed by a dynamic live band and stunning visual production, the show promises an immersive experience featuring:
Iconic Choreography – Witness the moonwalk, the signature spins, and the sharp, explosive dance breaks that revolutionized pop performance.
Note-Perfect Vocals – From falsetto highs to soulful ballads, the tribute captures the emotional depth and vocal range that made MJ’s music timeless.
Career-Spanning Setlist – Expect beloved favorites and deep-cut gems spanning decades of hits, giving longtime fans and newcomers alike plenty to sing along to.
Dazzling Costumes & Stage Design – Authentic outfit recreations and lighting design pay tribute to the visual artistry that made Jackson’s performances legendary.
Set inside the opulent, historic Landmark Theatre — with its ornate architecture and rich entertainment history — the venue itself adds a layer of grandeur to the evening, making it feel less like a tribute show and more like a genuine trip back in time.
Whether you’re a lifelong Michael Jackson fan who danced to these songs the first time around, or a newer listener discovering the magic for the first time, this show is designed to unite audiences in celebration of one of the most influential artists in music history.

event.title: Bert Kreischer: Permission to Party World Tour
event.description:
Bert Kreischer’s career has evolved from Rolling Stone’s infamous “Number One Partier in the Nation” to one of the top-grossing stand-up comedians in the world—and a powerhouse entrepreneur, actor, producer, content creator, and entertainment brand. Named by Forbes as “one of the best storytellers of his generation,” Kreischer has parlayed his signature comedy and authenticity into a dynamic media empire.

His sixth Netflix special, Lucky, filmed in his hometown of Tampa, FL, sold out all six shows within 24 hours of the on-sale and premiered in Netflix’s Top 10 Most Watched TV Shows in March 2025.

Through Berty Boy Productions, Kreischer oversees hit podcasts and series including Bertcast, Something’s Burning, and 2 Bears, 1 Cave (with Tom Segura), commanding over 16 million fans and 4 billion impressions. He also founded the Fully Loaded Comedy Festival, a touring juggernaut that’s expanded to stadiums, arenas, and sold-out cruises.

In 2024, Kreischer and Segura launched Por Osos Vodka, an award-winning, rapidly expanding spirits brand. Kreischer also starred in and produced Sony Pictures’ The Machine—a feature film adaptation of his legendary stand-up story—which broke into Netflix’s Global Top 10 Films upon release in 2023. His Netflix scripted comedy series Free Bert debuted in January 2026, and quickly broke into Netflix’s U.S. and global Top 10. The show drew millions of viewers in its first weeks, ranking among the platform’s most-watched series worldwide.

Today, Bert is on his Permission To Party World Tour and continues to blend comedy, business, and culture into one of the most recognizable personal brands in entertainment today.

event.title: Dr. Neil deGrasse Tyson – Cosmic Collisions
event.description: All the things that go bump in the night (and in the day). And yes, the universe wants to kill you: On occasion these collisions — asteroid & comet impacts on Earth, render life extinct. Learn why and how this happens, and what we are doing (or not doing) about it.

event.title: Theresa Caputo Live! – The Experience
event.description:
For more than a decade, Theresa Caputo—known worldwide as the Long Island Medium—has touched the lives of millions of fans, comforting supporters when they need it most.

Through personal life stories, candid humor, and intimate details about her gift to communicate with those who have passed on, the beloved television personality and best-selling author delivers healing messages to her audience, reassuring them with the revelation that their deceased loved ones are still with them—just in a different way.

Recognized as one of the most renowned mediums for over 20 years, Theresa Caputo Live: The Experience is the awe-inspiring event you won’t want to miss.

event.title: Hell’s Kitchen
event.description:
Contains some strong language and moments with mature themes.

Welcome to HELL’S KITCHEN, the hit musical from 17-time Grammy® Award winning Alicia Keys—inspired by her life, her music, and her community.

Your journey begins with Ali, a 17-year-old girl full of fire, searching for freedom, passion, and her place in the world. Along the way, you’ll meet the musical mentor who changes her life, her dynamic family, and the neighborhood that helps her grow. Relatable, raw, and refreshingly fun, HELL’S KITCHEN is a celebration of finding yourself, your purpose, and the people who lift you up.

More than watching a performance, this experience pulls you out of your seat and has you buzzing when you leave, wondering who to tell about it first. The music—a mix of Keys’ greatest hits and new songs written exclusively for the show—is brought to life through exhilarating choreography. It’s a soundtrack of rebellion, life, and love that speaks to you no matter where you’re from, where you’ve been, or where you’re going.

Hailed as a New York Times Critic’s Pick that is, “thrilling from beginning to end – a rare must-see!” HELL’S KITCHEN is directed by four-time Tony Award nominee Michael Greif (Rent, Dear Evan Hansen and The Notebook), with choreography by four-time Tony Award nominee Camille A. Brown, a book by Pulitzer Prize finalist Kristoffer Diaz, and the music of Alicia Keys.

Feel the energy of this multi-award-winning musical and experience where dreams begin: HELL’S KITCHEN

*Interpreters will be available at this performance

**Anyone, regardless of age, must have their own ticket.

event.title: New York State Craft Brewers Festival
event.description:
The 13th annual New York State Craft Brewers Festival returns to the historic Landmark Theatre in downtown Syracuse on Saturday, November 21st, 2026. The renowned event brings together 45+ breweries from every region of the state offering enthusiasts, both novice and seasoned, a rare opportunity to relish in unique and award-winning beer. Discover new styles, flavors, and brands, and meet the masters behind the craft you love! Brewery owners & representatives pour at the events, NO volunteers.

Great beer deserves to be paired with great food! Savory eats will be available for purchase from some of Syracuse’ best food vendors.

BACK BY POPULAR DEMAND! Upgrade to VIP for an exclusive NY Beer & BBQ Pairing at Middle Ages Brewing, taking place before the festival at 2:30 PM. This one-of-a-kind experience features a curated flight of New York craft beers each paired with a BBQ dish by the famed Dinosaur BBQ.

VIP ticket holders will also receive special festival glassware, VIP swag, and access to exclusive VIP-only brews at the fest. Don’t wait – only 80 spots available!

With over a decade of experience, New York State Craft Brewers Festivals are produced with highest level of care and professionalism, with the goal of providing a truly authentic craft beer experience for all.

event.title: Lindsey Stirling – The Snow Waltz Tour
event.description:
Multi-platinum, award-winning violinist Lindsey Stirling today announced the return of her Snow Waltz Holiday Tour, bringing her dazzling combination of music, dance, aerial acrobatics and theatrical production to audiences across the United States this holiday season. 🎄

$1 per ticket goes towards Lindsey’s foundation, The Upside Fund, which focuses on equitable healthcare and medical debt relief, mental health access, and nutrition education and food justice.

Set to Tchaikovsky’s iconic score, this grand production transforms the stage into an unforgettable celebration of the season — one your family will treasure for years to come. Get tickets now!

event.title: Sound of Music
event.description:
Tickets will go on sale to the general public on Oct 5th

For 65 years, THE SOUND OF MUSIC has been one of our “favorite things.” With its timeless story and irresistibly charming score, this Rodgers & Hammerstein classic isn’t just meant to be enjoyed – it’s meant to be shared. Now, a critically acclaimed North American tour brings the cherished musical to stages across the country to teach a new generation to sing.

Directed by three-time Tony Award® winner Jack O’Brien (Hairspray), this vibrant and romantic tale of Maria and the von Trapp family will captivate audiences with its universal themes of love, resilience and the power of music.

Featuring beloved songs like “Do-Re-Mi,” “Sixteen Going on Seventeen” and “Edelweiss,” THE SOUND OF MUSIC is the iconic tale of a spirited nun who chooses not to live behind closed doors – and, by following her heart, learns to climb every mountain.

THE SOUND OF MUSIC features music by Richard Rodgers, lyrics by Oscar Hammerstein II, and book by Howard Lindsay and Russel Crouse, suggested by The Trapp Family Singers by Maria Augusta Trapp. The 1965 Oscar®-winning film recently celebrated its 60th anniversary and continues to be one of the most successful movie musicals of all time.

www.SoundOfMusicOnTour.com

*Interpreters will be available at this performance

**Anyone, regardless of age, must have their own ticket.

event.title: Joe Bonamassa
event.description: Joe Bonamassa is one of today’s top live performers. His enthusiastic shows are one of the biggest parts of his career, and a favorite for music lovers worldwide. Hailed internationally as one of the greatest guitar players of his generation and cited by Guitar World Magazine as “the world’s biggest blues guitarist,” Bonamassa has almost single-handedly redefined the blues-rock genre and brought it into the mainstream. Backed by a stellar band of legendary musicians, the set list for this show will feature new songs alongside career-spanning favorites. By exceeding his own vertiginously high artistic goals, Bonamassa has shattered all expectations with 31 #1 Billboard Blues Albums (more than any other artist in history). Bonamassa’s career in the music industry has built steadily over the years and is only gaining more momentum.

event.title: Sonic Live In Concert
event.description:
Celebrate 35 years of one of the most iconic video game franchises of all time: Sonic the Hedgehog.  This new in concert experience brings together, live on stage, the most iconic music and incredible moments of the beloved Sonic video games. 

A live ensemble, rock musicians, electronics, and vocalists will perform an array of the incredible and defining songs from throughout the games as well as instrumental renditions of fan favourites from the Genesis era to now as they accompany the most exciting moments from across the games. From Green Hill Zone to “Undefeatable,” there’s no better way to celebrate Sonic’s rich history.

Audiences can expect musical Easter eggs woven into the arrangements and an electrifying production, adding an extra layer of discovery that brings Sonic’s world vividly to life on stage.

The concert also highlights the creative legacy behind Sonic’s music from legendary composers Jun Senoue and Tomoya Ohtani, whose work has helped define Sonic’s sound across generations.

This is a must-see show for Sonic fans!

event.title: The Wiz
event.description:
Individual show tickets are not available for sale at this time. Season tickets are available for purchase now. More information at: BroadwayinSyracuse.com 

This production uses haze, smoke and flashing lights.

The Tony® Award-winning Best Musical that took the world by storm is back.

THE WIZ returns “home” to stages across America in an all-new tour, direct from Broadway.

The Baltimore Sun raves “Powerhouse performances. Stunning choreography. Visionary sets” and the Chicago Sun-Times proclaims THE WIZ is “An eye-popping and high-intensity revival!”

This groundbreaking twist on The Wizard of Oz changed the face of Broadway—from its iconic score packed with soul, gospel, rock, and 70s funk to its stirring tale of Dorothy’s journey to find her place in a contemporary world.

With direction by Schele Williams (The Notebook, revival of Disney’s Aida), choreography by JaQuel Knight (Beyoncé’s “Single Ladies,” Black Is King) and additional material by Tony-nominated and Emmy-nominated writer and TV host Amber Ruffin (The Amber Ruffin Show, Late Night with Seth Meyers), this dynamite infusion of ballet, jazz, and modern pop brings a whole new groove to easing on down the road. Everybody rejoice!

*Interpreters will be available at this performance

**Anyone, regardless of age, must have their own ticket.

event.description:
The Rock Orchestra has become a global phenomenon, entertaining over 1,000,000 guests globally and charting at No.1 in the Rock and Metal charts with their first album.

Now they return to the USA to deliver a 90-minute spectacle.

The Rock Orchestra is a rotating collective of some of the world’s best musicians and vocalists, breathing beautiful dark energy into legendary rock and metal.

Performing the music of: Metallica, The Cranberries, Linkin Park, AC/DC, Evanescence, Rolling Stones, System of a Down, Guns n Roses, Korn, Led Zeppelin Papa Roach, Aerosmith, Rage Against the Machine, Nirvana, Hozier and more.

event.title: The Outsiders
event.description:
Individual show tickets are not available for sale at this time. Season tickets are available for purchase now. More information at: BroadwayinSyracuse.com 

The Outsiders includes flashing lights, loud noises, smoking on stage, and haze.

Due to the special effects, drops of water, washable red liquid, and small rubber pieces from the stage floor may land in the pit seating area.

The winner of four 2024 Tony Awards®, including Best Musical, is THE OUTSIDERS.

Adapted from S.E. HINTON’s seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA’s iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) and Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, and arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, and direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, “THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation.”

In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of ‘outsiders’ battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self-discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging…and the realization that there is still “lots of good in the world.”

*Interpreters will be available at this performance

**Anyone, regardless of age, must have their own ticket.

event.title: MAG Highlights Tour
event.cost: Free
event.description:
Drop in for a guided tour—no reservations needed! Led by an experienced volunteer docent, you will see highlights of MAG’s collection, from ancient artifacts to artworks of our time. Join the conversation and ask questions as you explore the museum full of art created by local artists and people from many cultures and places around the globe.

MAG Highlights Tours are FREE with museum admission and approximately one hour. Upon arrival, please come to the Admissions Desk and let us know that you wish to join the tour.

Public tours are subject to docent availability.

event.title: Mindful MAGiC: Candlelit Consciousness Concert
event.description:
Ignite your inner calm with an evening of sound and shadow! October 8th, step out of the daily rush and into the glow. Mindful MAGiC: Candlelit Consciousness Concert invites you to experience our auditorium as never before—filled with gongs and transformed into a flickering sanctuary of over 200 candles.

Harold Taddy brings the sound bath element of MAG’s celebrated wellness series to the main stage, weaving a tapestry of tranquil soundscapes. To help guide your journey, this performance features poetic guided meditations by spoken word artist Theo Trombulak woven seamlessly throughout the experience, creating a space that is as intellectually stirring as it is restorative.

Part recital and part immersive meditation, this is a rare opportunity to experience “concert-style” mindfulness in a supportive, beautifully lit environment.

This is a seated experience—just bring yourself. Less movement, more MAGiC—just you and the sound.

Important Program Details

  • All guests must be seated by 6:30 pm to preserve the tranquil nature of the session. To ensure a peaceful atmosphere for all participants, late entry will not be permitted once the session is underway.
  • Food and beverages are not permitted in the galleries. Please use the designated cubby spaces in the Vanden Brul Pavilion for storage.
  • This is a seated experience in MAG’s auditorium. Seating is arranged in a theater-style configuration, offering clear views of the stage and excellent sound quality throughout the venue. Guests may choose their seats upon arrival on a first-come, first-served basis. For added comfort, feel free to bring a blanket and settle in for the experience.

For questions about this program, contact Katie Nguyen, Senior Manager of Guest Services, at knguyen@mag.rochester.edu.

Ticket sales end on Thursday, October 8, at 6:15 pm. Ticket includes museum admission. Member discount applies to the first two tickets in your order.

event.title: Museum of the Dead
event.description:
Do you like scary movies? Museum of the Dead is back with all your favorite (slightly) scary experiences—art, music, a costume contest, cocktails, fortune-telling, and food—it’s the party you cannot miss! Sign up early for your chance to save on tickets to get in on more activities, more friends, more fun, more giveaways, and more scares this year.

Ticket sales are open for everyone! There’s a $10 discount on general tickets through October 1 (applied at checkout).

Buy general tickets

VIP Experience—SOLD OUT!

Want the ultimate Museum of the Dead experience? MAG’s VIP hour is back! Your ticket includes exclusive Scream-tastic swag, entry to the VIP lounge (with dedicated bar), a discounted ticket to the food trucks, a complimentary drink, and a VIP photo op. You’ll also be able to register for tarot card readings and ghost tours during the VIP hour, as well as a few spots during the rest of the night.

Tarot Card Reading & Ghost Tours

Timed-ticket alert! Be sure to sign up ahead of time to secure a time slot with our fortune-tellers or a ghost tour with Monroe County Paranormal Investigations. (There’s no additional cost to reserving a spot for a reading or a tour, but space for both is limited.)

The links to register are shared in the confirmation email sent when you buy tickets. Please note that the registrations links for VIP guests are different from the links for general admission; please use the links provided.

Schedule of Events

7:00–8:00 pm | VIP hour

7:00–11:00 pm | Food Trucks

8:00–10:00 pm | Museum Galleries open for exploration

  • 8:15–9:45 pm | Tarot card reading (by registration) in Renaissance Gallery
  • 8:30–10:00 pm | Organ concert in the Fountain Court

8:00–11:00 pm | Party in Cutler Union & Vanden Brul Pavilion

  • 8:00–10:00 pm | Arts & Crafts in the M&T Bank Ballroom
  • 8:00–11:00 pm | Movie: Scream, shown in the M&T Bank Ballroom
  • 8:00–11:00 pm | Live DJ & Dancing, Step & Repeat Photo Op in the Vanden Brul Pavilion
  • 10:00 pm | Costume Contest winners announced in the Vanden Brul Pavilion

Costume Contest

Throughout the night, MAG staff members will be giving out cards to guests who qualify for the costume contest. Save your card, and meet at the Admissions Desk/entrance to the galleries at 9:50 pm, with the costume contest at 10 pm. If YOU think you qualify for the contest, find a MAG staff member and let them know, they might just give you a card!

At 10:00 pm, everyone will gather in the Vanden Brul Pavilion, and the DJ will announce the winners. Winners will get great prizes from local businesses!

Categories:

  • Best group
  • Best couple
  • Funniest
  • Most mind-blowing
  • Spookiest
  • Most inspired by MAG art

Parking and Maps

Museum of the Dead takes place at the Memorial Art Gallery (see on google maps). We have free on-site parking in our parking lots and on the grass. It’s available on a first-come, first-serve basis; we recommend checking out other available free parking in the Neighborhood of the Arts (NOTA) ahead of time, in case our lots are full when you arrive.

Once parked, you will enter MAG through the Cutler Union entrance (please follow the signs. You will see stairs and will go up to check-in). If you need wheelchair access, please go through MAG’s Main Entrance, where Security will lead you to check-in.

Maps of the grounds and interior will be available soon!

Guidelines

We have some special guidelines to make sure this event is fun for everyone!

  • Please arrive with your proof of identification. This event is 21+ only, and we will be checking everyone’s ID at check-in.
  • Tickets will not be sold at the door. Make sure you and your friends get them early! Sales end on Friday, October 23, at 6:00 pm.
  • Please print your tickets or have them ready to be scanned on a mobile device upon arrival. This helps make check-in quick and easy!
  • Please be mindful of the props and substances used in your costume. To protect the works in our galleries, we will have a place set up to check the following items before exploring the collection: swords, sabers, wings, spider legs, potions, broomsticks, feathers, sticky/slimy/wet/glittery substances. Please note: there may be additions to this list at the discretion of MAG staff.
  • Please leave weapons (costume or real—guns, knives, etc.), backpacks, and water bottles at home.
  • Please remember that MAG is a non-smoking campus. This includes smoking, vaping, and any recreational substances.
  • Please arrive by 9:30 pm. We want everyone to make the most of their time with us!
  • Please remember that there is no re-entry.

event.title: Art Lover’s Tour: Santa Fe
event.description:
Join us in Georgia O’Keeffe country and delve into the rich heritage of northern New Mexico on a journey that weaves together centuries-old craft traditions with the splendor of iconic sights.

Enjoy opportunities to engage directly with skilled local artisans, art curators, and gallery owners, whose insights reveal how ancestral knowledge, materials, and cultural values continue to shape living artistic traditions in the Southwest today. Visits to museums, Abiquiú, and Ghost Ranch situate artistic practice within the dramatic terrain that inspired generations of makers, painters, and writers. A visit to O’Keeffe’s studio reveals the deep connection between the artist and the creative vision she cultivated there for more than four decades. In Chimayo, examine the continuity of devotional art, weaving, and vernacular architecture rooted in centuries-old Hispano traditions. Throughout, enjoy Santa Fe’s cuisine defined by the use of heirloom ingredients and deeply rooted regional flavors that feel both ancient and inventive.

To be added to the waitlist for this tour, contact Emily Whitson, Distant Horizons, at 562-983-8828 or emilyw@distant-horizons.com.

 

Tour Highlights

  • Enjoy a tour of the Georgia O’Keeffe Museum pairing iconic paintings with personal objects that illuminate her deep connection to the New Mexico landscape.
  • Meet with gallery owner Andrea Fisher, a premier authority on New Mexico Pueblo pottery who maintains close relationships with artists.
  • Go behind-the-scenes at the Museum of International Folk Art with Laura Addison, one of the world’s largest museums dedicated to folk art.
  • Basketry was one of the first craft forms practiced by Indigenous communities and learn about the various styles at the Adobe Gallery.
  • Be part of a curated visit to O’Keefe’s home at Abiquiú, and understand how the landscape inspired her with a visit to nearby Ghost Ranch.
  • Visit Evoke Gallery and meet with director Katherine Erickson. Evoke emphasizes contemporary figurative painting and representational art.
  • Visit the IAIA’s Museum of Contemporary Native Arts and be joined by Manuela Well Off Man, chief curator for a very special visit.
  • Explore the Santuario de Chimayo, the second most important Catholic pilgrimage center in the United States.
  • Accompanied by Patricia Trujillo-Oviedo learn about the weaving traditions of Chimayo. She is a seventh generation descendant of original local settlers.
  • Throughout the program, enjoy Santa Fe’s cuisine and deeply rooted regional flavors that feel are both ancient and inventive. New Mexico blends Native American, Hispanic, and Anglo traditions in dishes that celebrate locally grown ingredients.

Our ART LOVER’S tours are organized and sponsored by the MAG Council to benefit MAG and are open to all interested travelers.

For more information or a more detailed brochure, email Michelle Turner at mt1@rochester.rr.com or Emily Whitson at emilyw@Distant-Horizons.com. For questions or assistance, please contact the MAG Council at magcouncil@mag.rochester.edu or 585.276.8910.

Anyone unable to attend a MAG Council Art Tour must make their request for a refund by contacting the MAG Council Office prior to the event registration deadline. For international/overnight tour refunds, the policy of the managing travel agency will take precedence.

If it is necessary for the MAG Council to cancel an Art Lover’s Tour, all payments made will be refunded in full.

The Memorial Art Gallery’s tour operator, Distant Horizons, is a California Seller of Travel (CST #2046776-40) and a participant in the California Travel Restitution Fund. Information regarding the rights of California residents to make a claim may be found at tcrcinfo.org. California law requires certain sellers of travel to have a trust account or bond. Distant Horizons has a trust account.

event.title: Art, Death, and Fashion DeTOUR
event.description:
Advanced medicines, skincare creams, surgeries, and social media filters help us to stave off the idea of aging and death — but what have we lost in the process? Join fashion historian Brandon W. Brooks for a spooky season MAGsocial DeTOUR℠, as he examines the intersection of art and our former deathways. How is the ever-present reality of death reflected in art, fashion, and memory? How might art and fashion temper our anxieties surrounding death, or shape our grief for a lost loved one? Have we all forgotten how to mourn fashionably, or is it all just a bunch of hocus pocus?

To submit a request for ASL interpretation, please email access@mag.rochester.edu at least two weeks before the tour.

For questions about this event, please contact MAG Engagement Manager Jessica Gasbarre at jgasbarre@mag.rochester.edu. Ticket sales end on Thursday, October 29, at 6:15 pm. Ticket includes DeTOUR℠ and museum admission.

event.title: Chasing Rainbows: How We Talk About Color
event.cost: Free
event.description:
Color is one of the most foundational experiences we have as humans—yet our understanding about what color is, how we experience it, and how to talk about it is a bit squishy. Is aqua blue or green (or neither)? Does that change when you put aqua next to a blue or green? And if it does change, does that mean it’s still aqua? Science can provide answers—but what happens when the answers science gives us contradict our own experiences? Even artists who work with color all the time sometimes struggle with how to order, describe, and work with color. Is there a common language we can all use?

Join lexicographer and author Kory Stamper as she guides you through a kaleidoscopic journey through modern color science, color psychology, color naming and descriptions, and our perceptions about color using artworks in the MAG collection.

Kory Stamper is an author and lexicographer who has spent near 30 years thinking (too deeply) about how to define the words that define us. In her 20 years as an editor at Merriam-Webster, she defined everything from “blue plate special” to “god” and answered dictionary user questions on everything from what color “nude” really is to why it’s “toothpaste” and not “teethpaste.” She has written about her time as a dictionary writer in Word by Word: The Secret Life of Dictionaries (2017, Pantheon). Her moderate obsession with color began during her time at Merriam-Webster, and led to her second nonfiction book, True Color: The Strange and Spectacular Quest to Define Color—from Azure to Zinc Pink (2026, Knopf).

Lecture will be followed by a book signing in the Vanden Brul Pavilion until 8:30 pm.

To submit a request for ASL interpretation, please email access@mag.rochester.edu at least two weeks before the program.

Advance registration is required for this free event. Capacity is limited. Registration closes on Tuesday, November 10, at 7:00 pm.

For questions or assistance, please contact memberperks@mag.rochester.edu.

event.title: Make a Connection!
event.description:
We invite you to spark something new — whether it’s a friendship, a flirtation, or just a fun night out. Join us for Make a Connection!, an evening inspired by the exhibition Hugo McCloud: to everything there is a season.

This event brings people together to discover unexpected common ground. Come ready to mix, mingle, and maybe meet someone who brings a little extra color to your canvas.

What to Expect

  • Cash bar and complimentary light fare beginning at 6:00 pm
  • Quickfire presentations from 6:30–7:15 pm, where participants (or their loyal friends) take the mic for a 2 minute slideshow-style spotlight celebrating their best qualities (attendees can watch without participating)
  • Post-presentation mingling throughout the museum’s galleries, where the connections continue

Presentations

Feeling bold? Want to show off a friend or yourself? Promote yourself or your friends in a positive light with a 2 minute slideshow highlighting best features!

Don’t have someone to present for you? Don’t worry—submit a slideshow and we’ll present it for you.

  1. You must sign up in advance to reserve a spot as space is limited. Fill out our online form by Thursday, November 12, at 8:00 pm.
  2. Keep it fun, friendly, and positive.
  3. Feel free to include images, but make sure that they are appropriate (we have nudes in the museum – we don’t need to see yours).
  4. Keep it short and sweet—each presentation gets 2 minutes! See an example presentation.

MAG reserves the right to review all presentations prior to the event.

For questions about this event, please contact MAG Marketing & Engagement at jgasbarre@mag.rochester.edu. Registration ends on Thursday, November 19, at 6:00 pm. Ticket includes this program and museum admission. Member price is applied through a discount at checkout.

To submit a request for ASL interpretation, please email access@mag.rochester.edu at least two weeks before the event.

event.title: Mindful MAGiC: Sonic Yoga
event.description:
Begin your morning with a restorative experience that blends mindful movement and immersive sound for a powerful journey inward. Set in the serene surroundings of the Fountain Court, this special session features yoga and meditation led by Shanna Pagan and is accompanied by an immersive live soundscape from Harold Taddy (The Gong Situation).

What You Can Bring

  • Yoga mat, bolsters, and layers for comfort
  • Cozy socks
  • A water bottle with a secure, leak-proof lid (no straws)

Important Arrival Details

  • Doors open at 9:00 am
  • Check-in at the Admissions Desk no later than 9:15 am to get situated
  • Please arrive on time to preserve the tranquil nature of the session

The session lasts 9:30–10:30 am, followed by a 15-minute courtesy window to ease your transition into the day. Museum admission begins at 11:00 am when the galleries open to the public.

Come curious. Move with intention. Let the sound guide you.

For questions about this program, contact Katie Nguyen, Senior Manager of Guest Services, at knguyen@mag.rochester.edu.

Ticket sales end on Saturday, November 28, at 9:00 am. Ticket includes museum admission. Member discount applies to the first two tickets in your order.

Join the waitlist

Taught by: Independent (No Instructor)

This is for returning students who plan to enroll in the next session. This independent work studio time will allow for continuing projects and individualized support from rotating instructors. Students can sign up for as few or as many sessions as they want. Any work made during this time will be bisque for the next session.

Materials

Students will need to purchase clay for their own use. Clay in various varieties is available for purchase at the Creative Workshop for $18.00 per 25lb bag. Glazes and firing are included in the class price. Please bring an old kitchen-sized towel you don’t mind getting dirty.

Registration Information

Registration for this program starts on Tuesday, August 18, at 10:00 am for MAG Members, and Tuesday, August 25, at 10:00 am for Not-Yet-Members. Online registration ends on Thursday, December 10, at 3:30 am.

Programs with inadequate enrollment are canceled one week before the first meeting. We will attempt to contact you via email to find an alternative program or to refund your registration fee.

Learn more about classes in the Creative Workshop, including information about parking and the refund and cancellation policies.

event.title: MAG Highlights Tour
event.cost: Free
event.description:
Drop in for a guided tour—no reservations needed! Led by an experienced volunteer docent, you will see highlights of MAG’s collection, from ancient artifacts to artworks of our time. Join the conversation and ask questions as you explore the museum full of art created by local artists and people from many cultures and places around the globe.

MAG Highlights Tours are FREE with museum admission and approximately one hour. Upon arrival, please come to the Admissions Desk and let us know that you wish to join the tour.

Public tours are subject to docent availability.

event.title: StART with a Story
event.cost: Free
event.description:
Make something new at the Memorial Art Gallery! Create art with the Creative Workshop, drop-in for Story Time, follow a guided tour with a Museum Educator, and browse books and toys with the Charlotte Whitney Allen Library.

Free for all ages; no museum ticket required.

Schedule of activities:

  • 10:00 am–1:00 pm: Art-making projects for ages 3 and up. Last projects begin at 12:45 pm.
  • 10:15 am–10:45 am: Story Time.
  • 11:00 am & 12:00 pm: Half-hour, family-friendly tours with a Museum Educator. Sign-up for tours upon arrival.

For questions about this program, email the Creative Workshop at creativeworkshop@mag.rochester.edu.

StART with a Story is sponsored by the Rochester Area Community Foundation.

event.title: Third Thursday Concert—Musical Reflections on MAG’s Medieval Collection
event.cost: Free – $10
event.description:
leiken, voice & Doug Balliett, organ

On the third Thursday of each month, from October through May, the Eastman School of Music and the Memorial Art Gallery present varied concert programs by faculty and guest artists featuring Eastman’s Italian Baroque Organ. These Third Thursday Concerts are included with museum admission after 5:00 pm and are made possible by the Rippey Endowed Trust.

All concerts begin at 7:00 pm. Please arrive early, as seating is limited and available on a first-come basis.

Blue Cactus

Rooted in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, Blue Cactus got their start among the active honky-tonk circuit, developing an electrified twang that now branches out effortlessly into folk, alt-country, and psychedelic-tinged rock. Having released three records to critical acclaim, they have grown a cult following in the South and beyond, their introspective lyricism and blistering guitar techniques making the band potent in the studio and on stage. Their 2025 album Believer was hailed in Bandcamp’s Best New Country list and earned them slots on SXSW, Hopscotch Fest’s main stage opening for Geese and My Morning Jacket, and PBS’ new original series, Shaped By Sound. Blue Cactus have toured throughout the US, developing a dedicated cult following. From intimate clubs to major festival stages, Blue Cactus is known for connecting deeply with audiences wherever they go.

linktr.ee/bluecactus

 

Ramona & the Holy Smokes

Formed in 2022, Ramona and the Holy Smokes have seen their star rise in the region and beyond. The band–which includes Kyle Kilduff (electric guitar), Brooks Hefner (pedal steel), Jay Ouypron (bass), and Porter Bralley (drums)–had built a rapport playing together before joining Ramona, and in their time together have brought their talents to Ramona’s songs and song ideas, shaping and arranging these for a signature honky tonk sound. The band has performed regularly in the region, appearing at several Americana festivals including Red Wing Roots (2024), Rooster Walk (2025), and Bristol Rhythm & Roots (2025), and has opened for touring artists like Margo Cilker, Colby Acuff, Willi Carlisle, Redd Volkaert, Joshua Hedley, Donna the Buffalo, and Kashus Culpepper.

linktr.ee/ramonaandtheholysmokes

 

Anna Kimm

Anna Kimm is a Charlotte-based singer-songwriter blending heartfelt storytelling with a hint of warm, melodic country charm. Her music pairs honest lyrics with dreamy Americana textures and a soulful edge. As she steps into a new era, Anna is evolving her sound into a more crossover country style, weaving together classic country roots, indie influences, and polished pop sensibilities to create something both timeless and fresh.

event.title: MHS Annual Fundraiser Breakfast – October 1, 2026
event.description:
JOIN US FOR OUR ANNUAL FUNDRAISER BREAKFAST
Preserving our Past, Funding our Future

 
Date:  October 1, 2026
Location:  Trinity Presbyterian Church Fellowship Hall, 3115 Providence Road, Charlotte
Event Start: 8:30am

New this Year – 50/50 RAFFLE!
Feeling lucky? Join in our 50/50 raffle at the MHS Fundraiser Breakfast!
Half of the proceeds will support MHS, and one lucky winner will take home the other half.
Raffle tickets will be available for purchase at the event. Be sure to bring cash or check to participate! The lucky winner will be drawn during the breakfast. Thank you!

 

The Mecklenburg Historical Society will be holding its annual fundraising breakfast on Thursday, October 1, 2026 at Trinity Presbyterian Church at 3115 Providence Road, Charlotte, NC at 8:30am.

This year’s event will primarily support one of our most important sites, the Sugaw Creek Presbyterian Church and the historic cemeteries One and Two.  Cemetery Number One is one of the oldest city cemeteries in the country.  The church is the oldest in Mecklenburg County.

 
The Mecklenburg Historical Society has a team working at the church addressing the needs of the historic initiative.  Your support helps fund the above items.

The program will feature an engaging panel discussion on the progress and planned work.

 
Please click here to view the event flyer for details or to share with others.

event.title: 2026 Belle Meade Society Fall Dinner
event.description:
The Greensboro History Museum’s Belle Meade Society will have its annual Fall Dinner at the museum on Monday, October 5, 2026. The evening starts at 5:30 pm and includes dinner, wine and a presentation by Kevin von der Lippe.

Drawing from the research conducted for the book Greensboro Depot, local railroad enthusiast von der Lippe will discuss how photographs, newspapers, maps, railroad records, and materials from private collections were assembled to document the history of one of Greensboro’s best-known landmarks. event.title: Night Watchman Evening Tours
event.description:
|

Join Old Salem’s night watchmen on their lantern-lit nightly rounds as we investigate true stories from the records…stories of spirits and fires, of ruffians and corpses!

Experience the original building where these mysteries and tragedies took place, and step into a time of instability and many unknowns. Learn about Salem’s most famous legend, as well as stories you have never heard before. How did the early inhabitants of Salem grapple with the dangers and suspense of their world, and make sense of supernatural phenomena?

Grab a cloak and lantern, and join the night watch to see for yourself!

This exciting tour is our most in-depth yet, and is designed for suspense-seeking guests ages 10+. This is a partially outdoor walking tour, on uneven streets, and in buildings with stairs. The tour may be held regardless of weather conditions.

Six tours will be held nightly, beginning at 6:30 PM with the final tour beginning at 7:45 PM. The tour is approximately 60 minutes in length, and 12 tickets are available for each time slot.

event.description:
|

American colonists and Americans in the new republic experienced one constant: change. From changing political identities, geographic boundaries, and conceptions of freedom, American lives constantly evolved. This seminar will explore the ways that craftspeople and cabinetmakers navigated this ever-shifting political and social landscape and the ways that they reflected shifting American and European tastes and identities in their work.

You can join us in Winston-Salem or online for this two day seminar. Participants will engage in two days of lectures, including a keynote address by Dr. Tiffany Momon, Director of the Center for Historic Preservation, Middle Tennessee State University and Founder of the Black Craftspeople Digital Archive, as well as opportunities to participate in pre-conference workshops and a furniture open house in MESDA’s study galleries.

event.description:
|

Learn how southern women exercised power in the early American South.

At 2:00 PM, join us to learn about the Edenton Tea Party, one of the first organized women’s political protests in America. On October 25, 1774, a group of Edenton women led by Penelope (Padgett) Barker (1728-1796) pledged to boycott imported British tea and cloth in response to the Tea Act of 1774. News of their “tea party” reached London, where it was reported in the Morning Chronicle and London Advertiser on January 16, 1775.

Join Old Salem’s night watchmen on their lantern-lit nightly rounds as we investigate true stories from the records…stories of spirits and fires, of ruffians and corpses!

Attractions

NC by Train Holiday Express

Holiday Craft Zone

Scavenger Hunt

Christmas Tree Alley

Wander through a forest of uniquely decorated Christmas trees — each one full of festive flair and holiday magic.

Jingle Bell Dance Floor

Tickets

$12 / person in advance, $13/ person on event day. Limited tickets available nightly. Purchase online in advance or at the Bulls Box Office (Mon–Fri, 9AM–5PM) or call (919) 687-6500. Tickets required for all guests 3 and up. Get Tickets

Flex Ticket Add-On

$3/person – By purchasing a flex ticket add-on, you have the ability to exchange your ticket to a different night if something comes up! Just contact the ticket office at (919) 687-6500 before the gates open on the day you purchased and you can move your ticket to a new date! Get Tickets

Igloo includes admission, one train ride per person, an unlimited hot chocolate bar, cookie platter, and s’mores kit with private fire pit. Get Tickets [/vc_column_text]

Snowflake Suite (Suite 8): $35 per person, minimum 20 people, max 30 people

Frequently Asked Questions

FestiBull of Lights is open nightly from 5:30 PM to 9:00 PM. The last entry into the park is at 8:30 PM.

All tickets are general admission and include access to all free attractions, such as – Holiday Craft Zone, Photos with Santa & Wool E. Claus, Scavenger Hunt, Letters to Santa, Christmas Tree Alley, Fire Pits, Holiday Slide, Heated Holiday Lounge, and the Jingle Bell Dance Floor.
